target_customer: US consumers and small businesses shopping for auto insurance
problem: Comparing auto insurance prices is slow and opaque because insurers do not publish rates and each quote needs a long form.
business_model: free comparison site, expected referral or lead revenue (not stated in sources)

founders.name: Jason Traff
education: MIT Sloan (YC founder page; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in the December 2012 TechCrunch article. Later co-founder of Shipwell per the YC page.

founders.name: Darren Nix
founders.background_notes: Listed as a Leaky founder on the YC page. Later built Interviewed (acquired by Indeed per the YC page) and Steadily.

exit.acquirer: Navion Insurance (commercial insurance business, per Leaky's own closure notice)
exit.reason: The closure notice says Leaky stopped providing auto insurance prices on August 31, 2013 and its commercial insurance business went to Navion. The notice says it received a cease-and-desist letter roughly every two months.

competitors.name: CoverHound
competitors.what: Online comparison shopping for insurance, started in California

technical_complexity.rationale: Instead of scraping quotes, Leaky read insurers' state regulatory rate filings and modeled what each driver would pay, which needed real data work for a two person team (TechCrunch, 2012).

defensibility.rationale: Pricing models derived from public filings could be rebuilt by others, and insurers pushed back legally rather than licensing data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Insurers sent repeated cease-and-desist letters, which took the site down once in 2011 and shaped the product; Leaky closed in August 2013.

market_need_then: Car insurance is a large required purchase and consumers lacked easy price comparison. Leaky reported more than $300 million of quotes provided and over $40 million saved by users (its own closure notice).

branding.domain_note: Operated at the exact .com leaky.com (YC page); no purchase history found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and friendly: 'Insurance doesn't need to be scary' (YC description).

branding.community_and_virality: Press framed it as a Hipmunk for car insurance; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable one word name, but a leak connotation is odd for a financial product and no source shows brand driven growth.

pivots.from: Scraping and displaying insurer quotes, taken down after cease-and-desist letters
pivots.to: Predicting prices from state regulatory filings
pivots.why: Insurer legal pushback in 2011 (TechCrunch 2012-03 relaunch and 2012-12 articles)

outcome_analysis: Leaky pursued insurance price comparison by modeling rates from regulatory filings, raised a small seed in late 2012 and expanded nationally, but legal pressure from insurers recurred roughly every two months and the company stopped auto quotes on 31 August 2013, selling its commercial insurance business to Navion. No larger round followed the 2012 seed, and the cause of shutdown beyond legal friction is not stated in detail.
notes: TechCrunch says $675K in the body and $670K in the headline; CB Insights totals about $690K, leaving roughly $15K unexplained. Finsmes dates the round to November 2012, TechCrunch to December 2012. The Navion link comes from Leaky's own closure page plus one trade item (dig-in); YC lists 'Acquired 2013' while CB Insights lists dead, so the exit is partly a wind-down. Stage 'seed' is the label used by the sources. Competition list has one dated entry; other rivals found (The Zebra, Compare.com) started in 2012 or later and are excluded.
